contested_assumptions: The 250x range (4000 to 985000) reflects: (1) different population scopes (600000 vs global); (2) different dose thresholds included; (3) LNT model assumptions; (4) data quality. The 4000 figure is not minimizing; it applies rigorous methodology to specific study cohorts. The 985000 figure is not peer-reviewed.

thyroid_cancer_note: LNT assumes any dose however small has proportional cancer risk. Most regulatory agencies use it conservatively. Its validity at doses below ~100 mSv is scientifically debated. All of the above projections share this assumption to varying degrees.

contested_assumptions: At population-average doses of 9-31 mSv over 20 years (Chernobyl Forum populations) the LNT-projected increase in cancer rate is ~0.3-3% above the ~25% spontaneous lifetime cancer rate. This signal is below statistical detection threshold in most epidemiological studies. This is why Forum and UNSCEAR both emphasize that excess cancers 'will be difficult to observe.'
